verdict.tagline: Charming space exploration marred by clunky controls and physics quirks.
for_you_if: you enjoy open-ended resource gathering and automation
you can look past early control hurdles
not_for_you_if: you experience motion sickness from camera movement
you need reliable multiplayer matchmaking out of the box
you find fiddly inventory management frustrating

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the tutorial and initial guidance as lacking, requiring external wikis or videos to learn basic systems.

citations.review_text:
The tutorial is awful and the first hour was really frustrating - many (like me) will need to check YT videos to help learn how to play.  

But once I figured it out, I've been hooked.  I play on my computer exclusively with SteamController and it works great.  It's playable just fine on SteamDeck but the research tree font is way too small and can't be read.

For fans of survival and automation games, I highly recommend Astroneer.
This game is actually really fun! so many mechanics. One downside: very hard to get used to. I recommend reading the Astroneer Fandom wiki.

Absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game design.

This game has genuinely one of the worst user interfaces I have ever encountered in any form of digital media. It feels like the developers decided that “minimalist” meant removing every piece of information a player might actually need, then replacing it with a collection of vague, meaningless icons and hoping nobody would notice.

The main menu does not even label its submenus. You are expected to decipher a bunch of symbols that are nowhere near as intuitive as the developers clearly imagined. That same design philosophy infects the entire game: no useful labels, no clear explanations, no sensible guidance, and seemingly no consideration whatsoever for how an actual human being interacts with software.

There is NO tutorial, no meaningful onboarding, and no explanation of the game’s basic systems. Materials appear to have arbitrary relationships with other materials, but the game makes almost no effort to explain what comes from where, what machines you need, or how you are supposed to progress. Instead of learning naturally through gameplay, you spend half your time alt-tabbing to a wiki because the game cannot be bothered to communicate its own mechanics.

That is not “exploration.” It is not “player discovery.” It is developers outsourcing their tutorial and documentation to random people on the internet. A game should not require an external encyclopedia just to understand its basic crafting chain.

Even after you manage to fight through the miserable user experience, there is barely anything worthwhile underneath it. The gameplay is tedious, repetitive, and painfully boring. You gather resources so you can build machines that help you gather more resources so you can build more machines to gather more resources. The entire experience feels like busywork wrapped in a colorful art style, with all the excitement of sorting recycling.

I spent about two hours in this, but most of that time I was tabbed out googling how to do anything. I played it with someone and neither of us could figure out almost anything, it was just a frustrating mess with no guidance.

If you like resource management and basic survival elements that don't overwhelm you with difficulty, this is a great game for you. It runs well on every device I've played it on, and even lowered graphics settings maintain the appealing art style. Bugs can be found in a lot of places, however very few of them cause setbacks or major grievances. It's a tight experience that fulfills everything it sets out to do, and then some.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the user interface and recipe menus as confusing and difficult to navigate.

citations.review_text:
Calm version of Factorio, less confusing and more pleasant interface. However, not for long-term play in solo mode or with friends, maybe for few runs. In general, having activated at least one core of planet, and having built a large shuttle with a large amount of fuel - the game can be considered as complete.

The content of the base game is enough even without DLC.

Poor UX and story integration make this an uncompelling slog of a game.

I really wanted to like Astroneer. The terraforming is neat, but digging for resources is a chore and your extremely limited backpack space is so frustrating. Resource management in general is really tedious and annoying. Further, the exploration and mining quickly become boring and samey.

The diogenic menus are neat, but just about the worst UI I have ever experienced. Finding which recipe you need, where to make it, and what it needs is an exercise in frustration.

The help menus and tutorials are just a few screenshots that are overwhelming when you start and not accessible enough later on. You almost need a wiki on a second monitor to play this game. The only other thing telling you what you should be doing or why is some generic, uninteresting, unfulfilling quests that poorly fit in. I know there's some cool stuff but it's buried under layers of tedium.

I've gone to other planets. I've dug way down (not all the way to the core). I kept playing hoping it would get more compelling, but I've given up. This isn't my first time playing the game but I don't think I'll pick it up again.

Please hire a UX designer

claims.claim: Reviewers describe recurring physics glitches involving vehicles clipping through terrain or becoming stuck.

citations.review_text:
TLDR: 6/10 would recommend just hard to give it a higher rating due to minor bugs and glitches remaining from my first play in 2019.

Astroneer is a great game that is unfortunately let down by small but prevalent issues. The heinous camera, the crafting station interactions just not working despite being in proximity or the cursor either not responding to clicks or buttons pressed and just bizarre bugs. This isn’t just tonight but always noticed over years of play across platforms. Not to mention the fact that sometimes click and button inputs can be made without a human actually making that decision i.e. pressing a button in real life. The worst glitch I personally encountered prior to this review tonight, genuinely had me confused and increasingly frustrated with, when I discovered what happened. On the planet Atrox before leaving to depart to the planet Sylva the dynamite in my backpack just detonated. 
I tried to recreate this;
1-	I could not detonate it in my pack n
2-	I could not detonate it and then place it in my pack 
My first thought was this the “ghost” input glitch that activated the dynamite? Most likely as I’ve not been able to recreate this through any test pertaining to player or sensor/repeater input (no sensors or repeaters were present or even crafted on Atrox). 
The resulting event was dynamite (1) on the large shuttle was detonated destroying the shuttle via the dynamite (1) in the back pack I know it was the dynamite in the pack to detonate as it flashed red (visual countdown) to top it off a nanocarbon alloy was in my hands having been removed from the pack to be placed in the shuttle the only time the cursor was knowingly over the dynamite in the pack was when the nanocarbon was held. A half full soil canister a circuit board 5/5A and circuit board 5/5B were in the pack. An inhibitor, wide and drill level 3 were on the terrain tool. None of these items could have caused this when arriving on Atrox to investigate and retrieve anything,…

Overall, I give this game a 6.5/10. Great game design, good story, but decent for exploration. This is more of a factory building game rather than a space exploration game. Totally would recommend if that is your jam. The lore and story is very interesting, and the game doesn't take itself seriously. I love the inventory management and the UI's. Everything is completely diegetic and makes sense from a world building perspective. Very immersive world building.

I think the game could use a bit more optimization. If you just bought the game, make sure to go into settings and capping the frame rate. It is unlimited by default and that made my computer very hot!

The vehicles suck. I wish they handled the terrain a bit better. It's like the wheels are square and the vehicle has no suspension. Sometimes they clip through the floor.

One thing though is that items icons could be more distinct. Every resource icon looks very similar. Some resources symbols have really good design, but many do not. I would recommend numbering resources like elements on the periodic table or adding coloured symbols to make each resource more distinct.

I do not recommend this for solo playing at all, nor full price, we got it at 75% off. We're still having fun mostly because we're playing together. 

1. Dedicated server is effed, we can't make an independent server like in Conan or many other games so we can't come and go as we please when we have time, we can only play when  the host is online. False advertising, shame. :bell::bell::bell:

2. It has so many bugs still and is very grindy, but most annoyingly many bad UI/UX issues, if you thought the camera in BG3 was the worst enemy get ready for Astroneer camera glitching in a wall, and then you get catapulted with your rover into orbit loosing all valuable items, I have the screenshots to prove it.  

3. many quality of life improvements that should have been base game are DLC, that's just bad cash grabby behavior that should not be encouraged. 

4. there is no story or much of a lore which is not for everyone. maybe in future iterations now that they sort of have an idea how to make games like this they can try and appeal to a larger audience. and fix the many issues mentioned above.  

I suppose it's good there is no thirst, and hunger mechanics because this game has a steep learning curve with no tutorial as is. But gardening and cooking could have been more fleshed out than the narrow snail use. Maybe they'll do another DLC for that. :unamused: 
Personally I prefer how Concerned Ape from Stardew Valley has handled updates and improvements so I bought many keys to gift to friends. But this I can't recommend to all my friends. It's going to be a pain for some who are  open to buying and playing this. I can see why it had mixed reviews for a while. I am willing to change my review to a positive if points 1 and 2 are resolved. Dunno how they will fix point 3.

edit: played another 100 hours, found even more bugs. but the winch sort of works on the VTOL, the winch is also convenient to drag a 4 large rover convoy out of the center of the planet using jet pack and…

ASTRONEER is one of those rare games where I collected every achievement and still wanted more.

Yes, the game used to have bugs. Sometimes your rover didn’t drive on the planet — it tried to become part of the planet. And honestly, I’m not 100% sure that tradition is completely dead yet. Please, Starseeker, don’t inherit the family talent for eating vehicles.

But despite that, ASTRONEER is genuinely charming. Exploring planets, building bases, unlocking tech, getting lost, accidentally launching yourself into space — it all just works.

My only real complaint is that research and progression used to end way too fast. You’d start discovering cool objects and then suddenly realize: “Wait… that’s it?” The newer content helped, but I still wish the game had even more reasons to stay in that universe longer.

Very fun, very cozy, occasionally cursed by physics.

10/10 would lose another rover underground.

citations.review_text: A simple that is easy to pick up, but has depth in the late game. Early game is all about exploration and late game focuses on automation. It balances both beautifully. Really fun for groups that like different gameplay styles but still like working together.

Honestly a step up for survival crafting as a genre. 100% recommend.
Spoilers ahead for mechanics and items.

Pros:
- Engaging gameplay loop where crafting has a clear purpose and survival mechanics are simple yet will catch you out if you're not careful
- Voxel planets with painting options means you can reform the land to be whatever you want (shoutout to the person that made bongo cat out of soil)
- Exploration brings anticipation and is fully supported/encouraged by the tether/vehicle mechanics
- Making the higher tiers of craftables has tangible impact on the gameplay other than being just bigger or making progression happen a bit faster
- Creative mode actually lets you be creative - you don't just follow the normal gameplay loop with unlimited resources, you can do whatever you want (like building a space train lol)
- The visuals are genuinely beautiful
- Custom run/walk animations for different skins (the bubble one waddles a bit and swings its arms wide lmao)
- Perfect amount of player customization
- Progression is non-linear and planets all offer their own perks and charm
- Is even more fun with friends, but multiplayer is not a necessary facet of the game (except those achievements lol)
- The music fits the atmosphere and hugely benefits the experience, but also the music fits the experience and hugely benefits the atmosphere
- The sound design is crisp, noticeable, and never gets old
- Friggin sweet hoverboard with flowy movement
- Vanilla Adventure Mode gamemode feels fair in its consumption rates and time taken to achieve or find things
- I nearly forgot - the HUD is BUILT-IN TO THE PLAYER CHARACTER lol
- Above all: G A L A S T R O P O D S

Cons:
- A f$%king microtransaction in-game store? Come on, Soft Era Systemdorks.
- Camera-based Z-axis (elevation) controls for land vehicles and ironically also
- Boring flight controls/experience for VTOL/EVA
- UI elements are also in-game models and will sometimes not stay within screen boundaries or will be obs…

Only con is it is a bit of a grind after a while as you do mostly the same thing on each planet, (explore, dig, get resources, build), though they are all different biomes and have different stuff on them.

Not a bad game. Pretty enjoyable at the start. But it slowly feels to weigh down on you always having to move around far distances and different planets to build new bases over and over. Feeling as though you've left behind all your hard work as you move to the next one. It'd be like playing No Man's Sky without freighters, base portals, or trade hubs. 

The gameplay is equally simplistic and needlessly complex. It's very very easy to pick up a machine instead of put materials into it, or to randomly emote point at the ground instead of picking something up. The inventory "UI" can be pushed out of view or just position based on how much open space is around you, can hamper management in caves. The shuttle landing system is very unappealing, you only move in one direction across the planet's equator, can't move the opposite direction, can't go north or south. If you want to land on the north or south poles you have to turn the planet and pixel hunt until you can touch the landing zone you're aiming for. 

Realizing after mentioning it before, this is basically a much worse NMS. Very similar concepts, genres, gameplay loops, even the plots have some similarity (from the few quests I bothered to read) but with a lot less to do.

you go into a cave, the camera zooms in..... AND NEVER ZOOMS BACK OUT.... WTF
you go by a rock, the camera zooms in.... AND NEVER ZOOMS BACK OUT.... WTF
you even get close to anything, the camera zooms in.... AND NEVER ZOOMS BACK OUT....
you go into a crashed ship and the camera zooms in.... and all you can see is your but or crotch of your character and you can't loot or clear anything

come on this is basic game dev 101 and they still can't fix it

look the first few years, yea ok..... But it was a playable release Dec 2016!!!!!!!!! the money has been rolling in since then and they still can't fix the camera

and then there is the "feature" when your using the extraction tool and you mouse too close to the edge the game freezes, your mouse cursor goes somewhere way off screen,  the extraction tool gets perma-turned on, and you have to fight to get the cursor back on the screen (more micro freezes) and then destroy everything around you till the game finally realizes you let go of the mouse button 10 minuets ago and have been wildly clicking it to stop(and no it doesn't matter if its windowed or full screen mode)

these 2 worsening bugs and the fact that it is still COMMON PLACE that you start a new game play for a few hours, or even several time, and you go back to play your save and the save will not load and this has been an on going issue for YEARS and still not fixed.

TLDR: 6/10 would recommend just hard to give it a higher rating due to minor bugs and glitches remaining from my first play in 2019.

Astroneer is a great game that is unfortunately let down by small but prevalent issues. The heinous camera, the crafting station interactions just not working despite being in proximity or the cursor either not responding to clicks or buttons pressed and just bizarre bugs. This isn’t just tonight but always noticed over years of play across platforms. Not to mention the fact that sometimes click and button inputs can be made without a human actually making that decision i.e. pressing a button in real life. The worst glitch I personally encountered prior to this review tonight, genuinely had me confused and increasingly frustrated with, when I discovered what happened. On the planet Atrox before leaving to depart to the planet Sylva the dynamite in my backpack just detonated. 
I tried to recreate this;
1-	I could not detonate it in my pack n
2-	I could not detonate it and then place it in my pack 
My first thought was this the “ghost” input glitch that activated the dynamite? Most likely as I’ve not been able to recreate this through any test pertaining to player or sensor/repeater input (no sensors or repeaters were present or even crafted on Atrox).

A half full soil canister a circuit board 5/5A and circuit board 5/5B were in the pack. An inhibitor, wide and drill level 3 were on the terrain tool. This game used to be amazing. But with the addition of buggy patches and microtransactions it's no longer fun.

I have 100% this game.
I had fun playing alone, with friends, exploring new planets and gathering resources, getting ourselves stranded without fuel for the return trip home, died countless times, and even got DLC. I had so much fun, however, with the current way things are run with the devs I can't in good conscious recommend the game anymore.

With a new game already launching for prelaunch playtest, there are sill countless bugs and issues left in Astroneers that have remained unnoticed and forgotten from the devs despite the very vocal community asking for a fix, and it's been clear their focus is not to correct any of them. With FOMO, paid skins, and broken DLC, I no longer consider this game in my rotation that I return to play, it will remain in the cloud.
